inputs.source: support tickets, including tickets emailed in by contractors

instructions.note: The prompt directs the agent to reset MFA and send the temporary pass to the ticket opener, treating ticket opener identity as sufficient authority for an account reset workflow.
The prompt relies on analyst approval as the stated safeguard; no destination binding to the account owner is described.

controls.name: Service desk analyst approval in the queue tool
controls.decay_rationale: The queue blocks idp.reset_mfa until a human approves, but effectiveness is reduced by high approval volume and routine benign traffic. The gate does not bind the temporary pass recipient to the account owner and later send_external is ungated.

controls.name: Bind temporary pass delivery to account owner or system-of-record contact
Require analyst approval for temporary pass delivery destination
Verify requester identity before MFA reset when requester differs from account owner

findings.title: Confused deputy: untrusted ticket can trigger MFA reset and temporary pass delivery to the requester

attack_path.note: Contractors and vendors can email tickets in; requester is the email sender.
Agent looks up the target user profile and memberships.
Agent resets MFA after analyst approval.
Temporary pass is posted to whoever opened the ticket.

forecast.watch_signal: Approval gate removed or narrowed, analyst approvals per reviewer remain very high, or unattended step limits rise.

evidence.observation: The agent is instructed to resolve MFA problems by looking up the user, resetting MFA, and sending the temporary access pass to the person who opened the ticket.
Contractors and vendors can email tickets in, the requester field is the email sender, and the temporary pass goes to whoever opened the ticket rather than the account owner.
The analyst sees the exact target account, requester, and full ticket body before approving idp.reset_mfa.
Two analysts approve about 400 requests per shift and most are routine, so approval volume is high and fatigue is plausible.

recommendations.action: Bind temporary pass delivery to the account owner's pre-registered channel or another system-of-record recipient, never to the raw ticket requester field.
Gate temporary pass delivery itself with analyst approval that shows the exact recipient and delivery channel from the system of record.
Require out-of-band identity verification when the requester is not the account owner or when the ticket originates from contractor or vendor email.

findings.title: Property finding: approval gate fatigue on MFA reset queue weakens the human check on a consequential action
findings.residual_rationale: The rubric floor is moderate because a raw-action approval gate exists, but this design fact keeps residual at high: the same gate is operated at about 400 approvals per shift across two analysts, most are routine, and the queue therefore functions under extreme consent-fatigue conditions for a shared-service-account configuration action.

forecast.watch_signal: Per-reviewer approvals stay above about 20 per day or rise further, or approval is broadened to remembered/session approval.

evidence.observation: Two analysts cover the queue and approve about 400 requests per shift; most are routine.
The queue is a raw-action review gate for idp.reset_mfa, but the high volume indicates fatigue risk for a consequential configuration action.

recommendations.action: Reduce approval volume per reviewer or route high-risk reset cases to a distinct queue with lower daily volume and mandatory individual review.

stride_coverage.rationale: The provided design includes no capability for self-configuration, tool definition changes, or mutable prompt/runtime control by the agent.
The design shows a short bounded workflow with no loop, spend action, delegation, or open-ended runtime that would support a present denial-of-service case.
The artifacts do not describe sender authentication, anti-spoofing controls, or non-repudiation properties for emailed contractor or vendor ticket submission.
The artifacts do not state transport integrity, mailbox protections, or queue ingestion validation for inbound emailed tickets.
The artifacts do not say whether inbound ticket content is encrypted in transit or exposed in logs beyond the approval queue.
The described risk posture for this flow is identity misuse rather than service exhaustion, and no queue flooding or resource exhaustion controls are described.
This outbound flow sends a temporary pass to a requester; the provided design does not indicate that the flow itself can exhaust service availability.
The artifacts do not describe queue integrity controls, role restrictions, or whether queued approval records can be modified after submission.
The artifacts do not say who can read queued ticket text or whether the queue enforces least-privilege access to sensitive ticket contents.
No evidence is provided on queue capacity limits, throttling, or backlog handling, so availability exposure cannot be assessed from the design alone.
The design mentions approval presentation but does not describe whether action and approval logs are tamper-evident or otherwise integrity protected.
The artifacts do not say whether logs contain temporary passes or ticket text, or how access to those records is restricted.
The design does not specify retention, quota, or resilience properties for the audit store, so availability cannot be evaluated.
An audit record store is implied, but the artifacts do not state whether approvals and agent actions are logged with tamper-evident provenance that separates analyst, requester, and agent.

rating.rationale: Present inherent risk is critical because an untrusted ticket can influence shared-service-account directory read, MFA reset, and irreversible delivery of a temporary pass to the ticket requester. The only declared preventive control is a raw-action analyst approval gate on cap.mfa_reset, but approval volume is high, so rubric step 2 reduces the path by one tier to high and cannot protect the ungated delivery sink. Forecast is critical because autonomy_increase or control_removal defeats ctl.analyst_approval and returns the path to the critical inherent tier. Manual validation applied because scripts could not be run.

limitations: This assessment reflects the declared design and configuration in the provided artifacts, not observed runtime behavior.

No source code, identity-provider policy configuration, ticket ingestion controls, or delivery-channel configuration were provided, so sender authentication, exact credential scoping, and audit-log integrity could not be verified.
No explicit runtime logging or provenance artifact was provided, so repudiation coverage for approvals and agent actions is only partially assessed.
